issue_context.body:
### The problem

I get the following error message immediately after entering the code from the `com.simplisafe.mobile` error message:

![image](https://user-images.githubusercontent.com/119349591/204344596-f4b14b68-4782-45b0-a901-2e86ad25d579.png)

After it tries to set things up a few times, the error message stays on this:

![image](https://user-images.githubusercontent.com/119349591/204344832-57bfee66-d8bb-492d-976a-11b0aa97f62e.png)

I have MFA enabled and generated the code through a new incognito Chrome window.

My SimpliSafe system has two "homes" associated with it. When logging in with my phone, it always defaults to the first "home" that doesn't actually have anything in it. The second "home" in the list is my actual house with all of the sensors, base station, etc., and has interactive monitoring. The first "home" does not have interactive monitoring.  Could this be what's causing the issue?



### What version of Home Assistant Core has the issue?

2022.11.4

### What was the last working version of Home Assistant Core?

_No response_

### What type of installation are you running?

Home Assistant OS

### Integration causing the issue

SimpliSafe

### Link to integration documentation on our website

https://www.home-assistant.io/integrations/simplisafe/

### Diagnostics information

_No response_

_No response_

### Anything in the logs that might be useful for us?

_No response_

Hey there @bachya, mind taking a look at this issue as it has been labeled with an integration (`simplisafe`) you are listed as a [code owner](https://github.com/home-assistant/core/blob/dev/CODEOWNERS#L1031) for? Thanks!

<summary>Code owner commands</summary>


Code owners of `simplisafe` can trigger bot actions by commenting:

- `@home-assistant close` Closes the issue.
- `@home-assistant rename Awesome new title` Change the title of the issue.
- `@home-assistant reopen` Reopen the issue.
- `@home-assistant unassign simplisafe` Removes the current integration label and assignees on the issue, add the integration domain after the command.

</details>


<sub><sup>(message by CodeOwnersMention)</sup></sub>

---

[simplisafe documentation](https://www.home-assistant.io/integrations/simplisafe)
[simplisafe source](https://github.com/home-assistant/core/tree/dev/homeassistant/components/simplisafe)
<sub><sup>(message by IssueLinks)</sup></sub>

Thanks for reaching out. A couple of things:

1. Can you download [diagnostics](https://www.home-assistant.io/integrations/diagnostics) for your SimpliSafe connection? I'm guessing you can't (since the integration doesn't fully load), but appreciate your confirmation.

2. If you can't download diagnostics, what versions are your two SimpliSafe systems—V2 (the old style) or V3 (the new style)?

3. Can you enable appropriate debug logging, restart your HASS, attempt to set up the integration again, and share your logs? **Make sure you take a spin through and remove any information that you don't want posited publicly.**

```yaml
logger:
  default: critical
  logs:
    homeassistant.components.simplisafe: debug
    simplipy: debug
```

(After you get logs, you can change your logging back to how it previously was).

I only have one SimpliSafe system, and it's V3 and associated with the second address on my account. The first address on my account is for an old address. I accidentally created a new home when I moved out of that first home many years ago, and now I have no way of removing it myself. I've reached out to SimpliSafe just this morning to try and get it removed, but nothing yet.

As far as logs, there's a lot in there an while I don't think there's anything confidential, I haven't looked deep into them to make sure. I see a lot of info about pin, credit card info, etc. that seems blank, but don't know if I'm just overlooking it.

However, I think I can still give you the information you need. The log shows 2 subscriptions, which seem to correspond to my two addresses. Both have the same UID, 2184912. This seems to be the default integration title/name/whatever it's called. However, each has a different SID, the first (for the "old" house being 2205530 and the second for the "new" target house being 2183090.

As we can see, the first subscription is not activated:
![image](https://user-images.githubusercontent.com/119349591/204374103-349ca9b3-7d7a-4f40-9278-e4177d7386f8.png)

But the second subscription is:
![image](https://user-images.githubusercontent.com/119349591/204374302-fe7f7484-8aa9-46d8-9e40-9a3caea99f59.png)

Looking at the error message that popped up, it appears the integration is using the first subscription that is parsed from the result, so the one with the 2205530 SID.
![image](https://user-images.githubusercontent.com/119349591/204373824-1c1ca95f-9e18-4b90-995f-dd403736e85a.png)

Is there a way to make the URL contain the SID from the second subscription (2183090) be used instead? This would probably fix my issue.

Excellent detective work. I actually already check for activated systems (and skip over inactive ones), but I'm using a different key in the response JSON: https://github.com/bachya/simplisafe-python/blob/9df39e438ddc0cdedb19f62eef60cb6370345741/simplipy/api.py#L351-L353

What value does your first subscription have for that key?

The result for the first, "old" subscription:
![image](https://user-images.githubusercontent.com/119349591/204378520-2ad9c938-1898-4f1c-bb02-e1ab9c95c07e.png)

The result for the second, target subscription:
![image](https://user-images.githubusercontent.com/119349591/204380244-a6f16228-b72b-48c4-a0d3-b28ec440a9fd.png)

Both subscriptions have `subscription["status"]["isActive"]:True`, which is intriguing to me because the first subscription/address has no device or monitoring plan associated with it.

Without trying to tell you a way to fix the problem, it appears that `subscription["status"]["hasBaseStation"]` and `subscription["status"]["monitoring"]` do behave as expected between the two subscriptions, as well as the `activated` key (which shows 0 for the first subscription and a 10 digit number for my valid system).
Got it. There was a reason for using `isActive` somewhere in the past, but I can't recall why. I'll investigate and either way, will get a fix for this into the upcoming 2022.12.0 beta.

Awesome, thanks! Is there a target date for the release yet?

I'm sure `isActive` was actually used in the past. In fact, I used this integration for probably close to 2 years until they added all of the MFA changes with no issues. At one point the integration just stopped working (with the same issue I reported here), but I wasn't using HA all that much anyway because we were moving pretty frequently. Now that we're settled in at our new home, being able to set up my home/away and smart lock automations again will be great. I appreciate all that you've done to keep this integration running well!

> Awesome, thanks! Is there a target date for the release yet?

Beta is released tomorrow, final release is on December 7. I'll work to get this in by tomorrow!
